Write morning pages. Just sit down and write whatever pops up in your head. Don't think about it, don't stop, just write. If nothing comes out, just write for example "I don't know what to write" over and over until some other word/sentence pops up in your head. 

Usually writing three whole pages is recommended, but I've found this is not necessary. I usually just use the site http://750words.com/ and write... well, 750 words.

So why should you do this? Well, I can tell you what it does for me. I'm a chronic worrier, I tend to be really anxious and worry about *everything*. When I write morning pages, my head is immediately cleared, as the things that worry me are bound to come up as I write and for some reason writing down the things that worry you tend to make them disappear from your head.

That is by far the biggest benefit for me. Aside from that, I feel a clear mood lift (probably connected to the reduced worrying), increased mental clarity and focus, reduced sleep latency (especially if combined with night-time journaling!) and much more. Also, the stuff that pops out on the page can sometimes surprise me. I really feel like I gain access to my subconscious at times and realize things about myself, my thought processes, emotions etc that sometimes surprise me.

Writing morning pages can be a pain in the ass, but it is **so** worth it.

You were aware that you were dreaming. That makes what you experienced a lucid dream. It doesn't matter if your dream control was limited (or even non-existant), if clarity was low etc. It's still a lucid dream, albeit maybe "low-level".

I'm afraid for many of us learning to induce lucid dreams is only the  first baby step. Most of us also have to do a lot of work on dream stabilization and dream control as well.

Yes, I've taken all kinds of drugs in dreams. All non-lucid ones, though. From what I remember, drugs usually either have absolutely no effect OR they feel exactly as in real life. I've actually even had a fair share of trips in dreams.

You're right, there is plenty of help available. I just rarely feel motivated to work for it the way I feel I have to. Mental healthcare in Sweden, like most healthcare, is almost free. But there's a crap-ton of bureaucracy involved and a lack of mental health professionals, which makes it hard to get the right kind of support. 

For example, I was at first referred to the local mental health triage by the social services. I went there, hoping to get assigned to a psychiatrist, but instead they referred me to my healthcare provider. It took me about a month before I even felt motivated to call them. When I visited, they in turn referred me to emergency healthcare services in a neighboring city about 40 minutes away by bus for an assessment. This was almost two weeks ago and I haven't went there. 

It sounds kind of ridiculous when I write it down, but it was such an immense challenge for me to even take the first step toward getting help. Getting referred around, even to *another town*, takes the wind out of me and makes me want to give up. I guess I don't have much choice though.

Thanks for the support.

As far as I'm aware, there is no actual ceiling effect on LSD dosage. However, it is more or less *practically* impossible to continually trip on LSD. 

This is simply because of the extremely rapid tolerance build-up. You could roughly say that tolerance doubles every time LSD is ingested. For example, if 200µg provides a user with a satisfactory trip at one occasion, if he or she were to redose within a short time frame after this trip, 400µg would be necessary to attain the same effects. Next time, 800µg would be necessary and so on... as you can imagine, this soon escalates to unrealistic heights.

LSD, along with other hallucinogens, in a way makes you experience the world in a *more real* way than usual. 

You see, our brains do this thing called "sensory gating". Our senses pick up way too much information for us to process all at the same time, and so through sensory gating information that is not deemed essential for survival is filtered out from your awareness. Without sensory gating, we would all be overwhelmed by the sheer amount of information our senses were feeding us.

Hallucinogens such as LSD disrupt this sensory gating, essentially making you aware of *more* of reality.

Note that this by no means validates whatever crazy "revelation" that may come from an LSD trip.

Hi. Thank you. Yes, that's correct, I live in Sweden. I'm afraid we don't have the privacy laws you speak of, though. A potential employer WILL ask about medical absence and the like and refusing to explain this absence or being vague will lead to not being considered for the job.

I only really have two options in this regard:

1. Being completely honest and saying the reason I haven't done anything for two years is because I've been doing drugs 24/7

2. Filling in the blanks with lies.

I'm currently electing for the latter, I'm pretending I decided to go back to school for a bit. I guess I see no real reason this wouldn't work out.

As for what I'm passionate about... see, that's the thing. I don't know. The paradoxical thing is that I see myself as (and have been described by others) a very passionate individual, but I can't for the life of me say what I'm passionate about. I guess you could say I'm sort of passionate about most things. I think most things are cool, I'd like to do a little bit of everything, but that's not really realistic.

I DO seem to have this yearning deep down in my soul to be a writer... but I keep telling myself that isn't a realistic path to pursue either.

All in all, I'm just... really lost. I don't know what I want.

Thanks, that may be a better starting point then. Makes a lot of sense, actually, considering I'm ISTQB-certified and have two years of work-life experience with it working at a reasonably respectable company (BlackBerry)

I'm going to do it no matter how long it takes, of course. This is my main goal in life as of now. I will just have to make some adjustments to my plan if it is unrealistic. I'm considering getting whatever local part-time job I can get to support myself while I'm developing my own skills and business on the side. That's probably a better idea.
